title: Serre comparison for the graded section module
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $\mathcal G$ be a coherent [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal O_P$-module, write $\mathcal G(n)=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(n)$ for the twists by $\mathcal O_P(n)$ of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], put $M_{\ge 0}=\bigoplus_{n\ge 0}\Gamma(P,\mathcal G(n))$ with its graded $S$-module structure, and let $\widetilde{M_{\ge 0}}$ be the associated sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The canonical morphism $\widetilde{M_{\ge 0}}\to\mathcal G$, whose restriction on each standard open $D_+(f)$ is induced by degree-zero localization of sections, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Stacks Project, Proposition 0BXD (coherent-proposition-coherent-modules-on-proj), last paragraph of the proof

proof.text: The standard opens $U_i=D_+(x_i)$ for $i=0,1$ cover $P$ by the definition of $\operatorname{Proj}S$ and [def-sc-p1-standard]. On $U_i$, the associated sheaf of a graded module has sections given by degree-zero homogeneous localization: for $N=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(P,\mathcal G(m))$, [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] identifies $\Gamma(U_i,\widetilde N)$ with $N_{(x_i)}$.

source.place: Definition 01M6 (associated sheaf on Proj), Lemma 01M7 (2),(3), and Section 01ND for the standard cover

proof.text: The localization $N_{(x_i)}$ is unchanged if $N$ is replaced by its nonnegative truncation $M_{\ge0}$. Indeed, a homogeneous fraction $t/x_i^r$ of degree zero with $t\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal G(r))$ already lies in $M_{\ge0}$; if a representative has negative degree, multiplying numerator and denominator by a sufficiently large power of $x_i$ gives an equal representative with nonnegative numerator degree. Thus $\widetilde{M_{\ge0}}|_{U_i}$ has the same sections and restriction maps as $\widetilde N|_{U_i}$.

source.place: Proposition 0BXD (coherent-proposition-coherent-modules-on-proj), last paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-invertible-section-localization] to $X=P$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_P(1)$, $s=x_i$, and $\mathcal F=\mathcal G$. Its hypotheses hold: $P$ is quasi-compact, being the union of the two affine (hence quasi-compact) charts $U_0,U_1$ of [def-sc-p1-standard]; their intersection $U_{01}$ is affine, so by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] (2) $P$ is quasi-separated and by (1) of that lemma the intersection of any two affine opens of $P$ is quasi-compact; $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is invertible and $x_i\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ by [lem-sc-p1-twist-multiplication]; and $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], since $\mathcal G$ is coherent and $P$ is locally Noetherian (covered by $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$). By [lem-sc-p1-twist-multiplication], the non-vanishing locus $P_{x_i}$ is $D_+(x_i)=U_i$, and the isomorphisms $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal G(n)$ identify the graded module $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(P,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n})$ of [lem-sc-p1-invertible-section-localization] with $N$, multiplication by $x_i$ corresponding to multiplication by $x_i\in S_1$. Therefore the canonical degree-zero localization map is an isomorphism $N_{(x_i)}\cong\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal G)$. Under the identification in the preceding step, this is exactly the canonical map $\Gamma(U_i,\widetilde{M_{\ge0}})\to\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal G)$ induced by localization.

source.place: Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), and coherent.tex Proposition 0BXD proof

proof.text: The two local maps agree on $U_0\cap U_1$: both send a localized homogeneous section to its restriction tensored with the corresponding inverse power of the same section $x_i$, and the localization maps commute with further localization. Hence they glue to the canonical morphism $\widetilde{M_{\ge0}}\to\mathcal G$ described in the statement. It is an isomorphism because its restriction to each member of the cover $U_0,U_1$ is an isomorphism.
